I will not start from empty talk. I will do it the way I have done for years, then change a little where it makes sense. On my 20 mu, I will keep most land in wheat-maize, because that is the steady road here and I have well water, so I am not afraid to push fertilizer a bit. I would rather spend some extra on fertilizer than watch the crop go yellow and lose harvest. I will leave 5 mu for cotton, because cotton still gives me some cash, but I will not put too much land there since it takes more watching and more spraying. For wheat and maize, I will mostly follow what people around me do when they get good grain: decent seed, enough bottom fertilizer, then one topdressing at the key time, and water when the crop is asking for it. I do not like gambling on low fertilizer. If I cut one bag and the yield drops, that hurts more than the saved money. So I will keep the wheat-maize land fed, use hybrid maize seed, use improved wheat and cotton seed, plough the cotton ground clean, rotary the wheat ground, and do no-tillage or light direct seeding for maize after wheat if I need to catch time. That way I save labor, keep the season tight, and still hold yield.
